RE: Level 1 Member Appeal – Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-11
Reference number: POC-D52DAC7115-38519
Requested service: Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
Treating surgeon: Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

Dear Member Rights and Appeals Review Team:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-11. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am submitting this appeal, together with my complete clinical record, within the 180-day appeal window identified in that notice (deadline 2027-02-07).

Blue Cross NC's own posted medical policy, "Surgery for Femoroacetabular Impingement," states that arthroscopic treatment of femoroacetabular impingement "may be medically necessary when all of the following conditions have been met," and that "BCBSNC will provide coverage for Arthroscopic Surgery for Femoroacetabular Impingement when it is determined to be medically necessary because the criteria and guidelines shown below have been met." I have not been able to obtain the complete, currently in-force text of this policy directly from Blue Cross NC's website, so beyond the phrases quoted above — which I did retrieve from Blue Cross NC's own policy page — I am not quoting any further policy language as the plan's own wording. Where I reference additional criteria categories below (age/skeletal maturity, symptom duration and severity, conservative-therapy trial, imaging findings, and absence of advanced joint damage), I am describing them in my own words based on the general framework that Blue Cross NC's policy page indicates is used, and I am specifically requesting that Blue Cross NC send me or my surgeon's office the complete, current text of this policy (including its effective date and full criteria list) so that we can confirm every element has been addressed.

With that framework in mind, here is how my clinical record addresses each area of medical necessity that a hip arthroscopy determination would reasonably need to evaluate, and I ask the reviewer to consider this complete packet in place of whatever was found "incomplete" in the original submission:

1. Skeletal maturity / age
[Patient's date of birth and/or documentation of growth-plate closure was not included in the clinical summary provided to me for this appeal.] Please confirm this is on file, or advise if additional documentation of skeletal maturity is needed; I will supply it promptly.

2. Duration and severity of symptoms
I have had 18 months of progressive hip pain that has not resolved with rest. I have sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, and I am unable to run or squat because of this pain. On examination, I have a positive provocative test on the affected side and pain-limited range of motion.

3. Failed conservative therapy
I completed a 12-week, physician-supervised course of physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification, from 2026-03-31 to 2026-06-23 (20 visits completed), as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. I also trialed NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-28 that gave only about 3 weeks of partial relief. This represents a sustained, well-documented, multi-modality conservative treatment course that did not adequately resolve my symptoms.

4. Imaging findings
An MRI arthrogram of the hip performed 2026-07-13 shows an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees. The joint space is preserved, with a Tönnis grade of 0, indicating no evidence of advanced osteoarthritis.

5. Absence of contraindications
I have no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder. My BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker.

Enclosed with this appeal (or available on request from Dr. Lindqvist's office) are:
- The physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-31 through 2026-06-23, 20 visits)
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial, corticosteroid injection 2026-04-28)
- The 2026-07-13 MRI arthrogram report
- Clinic notes documenting history, physical exam findings (including provocative testing), and functional limitations
- [A letter of medical necessity from Dr. Lindqvist, if not already on file]
- [Documentation of skeletal maturity/age, if requested]

Because Blue Cross NC's denial letter did not specify which particular document or data element was considered missing, I am also formally requesting, under my right to the information relied upon in this determination, that Blue Cross NC identify precisely what documentation was found incomplete, and provide me or my provider with a copy of the specific medical policy and clinical review criteria applied to CPT 29914 in my case, including its policy number (if any), effective date, and full text, so that we can ensure full compliance if any gap remains.

I ask that Blue Cross NC reverse the denial and authorize the requested hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) based on the complete documentation now provided. If any single item above is still considered insufficient, please contact me or Dr. Lindqvist's office at [surgeon's office phone/fax] directly so it can be supplied before a final appeal decision is made.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Emerson Hayes
